prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1045; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured after a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The insured reports neck and shoulder pain and says the claimant's vehicle was stopped in front of them when the impact occurred. The driver is confirmed as a named driver on the policy.

Entry 2: Claimant is now represented by counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office. A letter of representation has been received and logged. Medical authorization requests have been sent.

Entry 3: Statements from two witnesses, scene photographs and the other driver's account all agree that the collision happened as the insured described. Initial damage estimate reviewed; the damage is mostly consistent with the reported impact speed and direction.

Entry 4: Claimant's recorded statement was taken today. Some details were added compared with the first report, but the core account has not changed. It is still not fully clear from the statement or the photos where in the vehicle the claimant was seated at impact.

Entry 5: A neighbor has told us they believe the vehicle had body damage several weeks before the claimed date. We have no independent record of earlier damage to the vehicle, and no prior claims on it are on file. The neighbor's comment has been noted for follow-up.

Entry 6: Medical records show a shoulder injury that is plausible for a collision of this type. Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the records received so far.
